summary: George Le Grand Jacob (1805–1881) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Elizabeth College and under John Borthwick Gilchrist, later serving as a teacher at Addiscombe Military Seminary from 1833 to 1835.

George Melville Bolling (1871–1963) was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Loyola University Maryland and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, he taught at Catholic University of America (1893–1913) and Ohio State University (1914–1940), and co-founded the Linguistic Society of America.

George Morrison Carstairs (1916–1991) studied at the University of Edinburgh, earning a B.M. and Dr.Med. He served as Professor of Psychological Medicine at Edinburgh (1961–1973) and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of York (1973–1978).

George Payn Quackenbos (1879–1947) worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his A.B. and Ph.D. at Columbia University and served as an Instructor in Latin at the City College of New York in 1910.

George Perrigo Conger (1884–1960) worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Cornell, Union Theological Seminary, Berlin, Jena, Heidelberg, the Sorbonne, and Columbia. He served as Assistant Professor at the University of Minnesota (1920–1952) and held visiting professorships.

George Quasha (born 1942) works in religious studies, Tibetology, and other fields. He founded Station Hill Press and has taught at Stony Brook University (~1968–1971), Bard College, The New School, and Naropa University.
George R. Elder is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Alex Wayman (attested 1978).
George Read Edward Beresford (1815–1857) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Manager at Cawnpore Bank until 1849 and as manager at Delhi Bank beginning in 1849.
George Rupp (born 1942) is a religious studies scholar who studied at Princeton, Yale, and Harvard. He held positions at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (~1993–2002).

George Rusby Kaye (1866–1929) worked in Indology and history/archaeology after studying at Wyggeston Grammar School and St. Mark's College. He held school posts in India, served at the Bureau of Education, and catalogued manuscripts at the India Office.
George Saintsbury (1845–1933) studied at King's College School and Merton College. He held a post at the University of Edinburgh from approximately 1895 to 1915.

George Santayana (1863–1952) was a philosopher who studied at Harvard under William James, as well as in Berlin and Cambridge. He was a member of the philosophy faculty at Harvard University from 1907 to 1912.

George Scott Robertson (1852–1916) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Westminster Hospital, he held posts in the Indian Medical Service (1878) and the Foreign and Political Department (1888).

Linguist and Indologist George Sherman Lane (1902–1981) studied at Iowa, Paris, and Chicago, working with Carl Darling Buck. He held positions at Chicago, Catholic University of America (1934–1937), and the University of North Carolina (1937–1972).

George Shirt (1843–1886) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Cambridge and the Church Missionary Society College. He became a missionary for the Church Mission Society in 1866 and a Fellow at the University of Mumbai.

George Smith (1833–1919) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who earned an LL.D. from the University of Edinburgh. He served as Professor at Doveton College in 1854 and was a Fellow at the University of Calcutta (1856–1875).

George Speirs Alexander Ranking (1852–1934) worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Aldenham School and Cambridge, he was Lecturer in Persian at Balliol College (1905–1920) and Professor of Persian at the University of Calcutta (1920–1922).

George Thibaut (1848–1914) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated in Berlin and Heidelberg. His career in India included leadership roles at Queen's College, Benares, Muir Central College, Government Sanskrit College, and a professorship at the University of Calcutta.
George Turnbull Marshall (1803–1854) was an Indologist. He served as Secretary at Fort William College from 1838 to 1852 and as Secretary at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1839 to 1840.

George Turnour (1799–1843) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service starting in 1818, becoming Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue in 1820.
